data.why: The app has no upload feature; it works entirely off a precomputed ~300-400MB SQLite DB (NCBI/ENA/Annotrieve coverage data) and an ETE3 NCBI-taxonomy DB that the app itself would normally fetch from GitHub Releases on first launch. Since the server has no network once running, both are fetched by curl during install instead: eukaryotes.db goes to the repo root (src/constants.DB_PATH) with no .version sidecar, so src/utils.ensure_latest_database treats it as a pre-existing, app-managed-as-is file and skips all network/version checks at runtime; taxa.tar.gz is extracted to $HOME/.etetoolkit/taxa.sqlite(+.traverse.pkl), the default path ete3's NCBITaxa() looks for, so the very first root-taxon selection (which calls NCBITaxa() to resolve name/rank) doesn't trigger a live taxdump build.

goals: Pick a clade (e.g. Mammalia, or any NCBI Taxon ID) and see at a glance what fraction of its species have a genome assembly, a functional annotation, short-read RNA-seq, or long-read RNA-seq.
Break the clade down by taxonomic rank (phylum through species) to find well-sampled versus under-sampled lineages before designing a comparative genomics study.
Filter to taxa matching a combination of resources (e.g. 'has an assembly AND long-read RNA-seq') to spot data gaps for a grant proposal or reading list.
Sort the breakdown by a coverage metric and limit to the top N taxa to prioritize which lineages to investigate further.
Visualize the breakdown as a phylogenetic tree with per-taxon divergent coverage bar charts, downloadable as SVG, to see where coverage clusters across the tree.
Export the complete, unfiltered breakdown as a TSV for downstream analysis outside the app.

review.summary: The goal and the first two phases match the README's stated purpose closely: survey assembly, annotation and RNA-seq coverage across a clade, break it down by rank, filter, sort, and see it on a tree. The labels are good and every screen I sampled supports its node. It should not be filed yet: the table view and both TSV exports, which are the README's main route out of the tool, are missing because of a NumPy/pyarrow version clash in the setup, and f3 bundles two separable components.
